what: US Democrat Ro Khanna says he was detained by armed Israeli settlers

clean_source_blocks.text: Ro Khanna pictured during a visit to Turmus Ayya, near Ramallah in the occupied West Bank on Thursday US congressman Ro Khanna says he was detained for 90 minutes by armed Israeli settlers during a visit to the occupied West Bank. Khanna, 49, had been in a van with his team when they were surrounded by settlers wielding M4 rifles on Wednesday, he told Reuters news agency. Writing on X, Khanna said that when the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) arrived, "they sided with the settlers and continued our detention". The BBC has reached out to the IDF for comment. The Israeli military said in a statement troops and police officers took action after getting a report settlers had blocked vehicles in the area. Israeli police officer filmed throwing stun grenade into car in West Bank

Ro Khanna said settlers were armed with US-made weapons and Israel Defense Forces refused to intervene The US congressman Ro Khanna says armed Israeli settlers detained him during a visit to the Israel-occupied West Bank recently, describing the experience as a first-hand view of the realities faced by Palestinians living under occupation. In an interview with Reuters on Thursday from a Palestinian village, the progressive US House Democrat from California said his detention happened the previous day while his delegation visited an area of the southern West Bank that has experienced repeated attacks by Israeli settlers. Khanna recounted how settlers carrying US-made M4 rifles surrounded the group’s van. “We were at a village that Israeli settlers had destroyed – they had destroyed the school, they had destroyed that village, and we were just looking at it,” Khanna said.
Khanna, 49, was visiting the occupied West Bank when he was held for 90 minutes, he says.

"Upon their arrival, the troops dispersed the Israeli civilians and allowed the vehicles to continue on their way," the IDF said. Khanna was visiting the ruins of Khirbet Zanuta, on a fact-finding visit to look at the impact of Israeli occupation of the area. The politician, a father-of-two, is mulling over a presidential run in 2028. "We were at a village that Israeli settlers had destroyed, they had destroyed the school, they had destroyed that village, and we were just looking at it," he said. "And these hoodlums come in with machine guns – M4, an American-made machine gun – and they detain us. They block off the road. And then they call the IDF and ​the IDF is on their side, not on the side of the Americans," Khanna said.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Ro Khanna pictured during a visit to Turmus Ayya, near Ramallah in the occupied West Bank on Thursday

US congressman Ro Khanna says he was detained for 90 minutes by armed Israeli settlers during a visit to the occupied West Bank.

Khanna, 49, had been in a van with his team when they were surrounded by settlers wielding M4 rifles on Wednesday, he told Reuters news agency.

Writing on X, Khanna said that when the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) arrived, "they sided with the settlers and continued our detention".

The BBC has reached out to the IDF for comment. The Israeli military said in a statement troops and police officers took action after getting a report settlers had blocked vehicles in the area.

Israeli police officer filmed throwing stun grenade into car in West Bank

"Upon their arrival, the troops dispersed the Israeli civilians and allowed the vehicles to continue on their way," the IDF said.

Khanna was visiting the ruins of Khirbet Zanuta, on a fact-finding visit to look at the impact of Israeli occupation of the area.

The politician, a father-of-two, is mulling over a presidential run in 2028.

"We were at a village that Israeli settlers had destroyed, they had destroyed the school, they had destroyed that village, and we were just looking at it," he said.

"And these hoodlums come in with machine guns – M4, an American-made machine gun – and they detain us. They block off the road. And then they call the IDF and ​the IDF is on their side, not on the side of the Americans," Khanna said.

While they were detained, an aide who was with Khanna said they made appeals to the US Embassy in Jerusalem for help, and were released after a group of police officers intervened.

Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem - land Palestinians want, along with Gaza, for a hoped-for future state - during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them.

The settlements are illegal under international law.

---

[Lähde: The Guardian]
Ro Khanna said settlers were armed with US-made weapons and Israel Defense Forces refused to intervene

The US congressman Ro Khanna says armed Israeli settlers detained him during a visit to the Israel-occupied West Bank recently, describing the experience as a first-hand view of the realities faced by Palestinians living under occupation.

In an interview with Reuters on Thursday from a Palestinian village, the progressive US House Democrat from California said his detention happened the previous day while his delegation visited an area of the southern West Bank that has experienced repeated attacks by Israeli settlers.

Khanna recounted how settlers carrying US-made M4 rifles surrounded the group’s van.

“We were at a village that Israeli settlers had destroyed – they had destroyed the school, they had destroyed that village, and we were just looking at it,” Khanna said.

Referring to the Israel Defense Forces, which is funded in part by US military aid, Khanna continued: “And these hoodlums … detain us. They block off the road. And then they call the IDF and the IDF is on their side, not on the side of the Americans.”

Khanna also told Reuters, “I saw the arrogance in the eyes of those settlers, 21- and 22-year-olds with guns, laughing that they had detained us, the arrogance of those young IDF soldiers that my tax dollars are funding – having no respect for the fact that they were detaining Americans, no respect that there was an American congressperson in that bus, and laughing when our translator told them that there are Americans there and the American embassy is concerned.”

Khanna added that the encounter illustrated “the arrogance of power – of a power that has had no accountability, total impunity – and it’s created a toxic culture of oppression”.

The New York Times first reported Khanna’s account on Saturday morning. He told the outlet: “I felt powerless in that situation, which is not an easy thing, as I have a lot of privilege in life.

“Imagine how people feel every day, Palestinians under the occupation, if they could make an American congressperson feel powerless for 90 minutes.”

Khanna said he and his group were ultimately able to continue traveling after contacting the US embassy and Israeli police.

The Israeli military said troops and police responded after receiving a report that settlers were obstructing vehicles near Khirbet Zanuta, according to Reuters.

Khirbet Zanuta is a Palestinian hamlet whose residents were forced to leave

payload.title: Ro Khanna kertoo aseistautuneiden israelilaissiirtokuntalaisten estäneen seurueensa matkan Länsirannalla
payload.summary: Yhdysvaltalaisen demokraattikongressiedustajan Ro Khannan mukaan M4-kiväärein aseistautuneet israelilaissiirtokuntalaiset saartoivat hänen seurueensa auton ja estivät sen matkan noin 90 minuutiksi miehitetyllä Länsirannalla. Israelin asevoimat kertoo joukkojensa hajottaneen israelilaiset ja päästäneen ajoneuvot jatkamaan matkaa.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain demokraattipuoluetta edustava kongressiedustaja Ro Khanna kertoo aseistautuneiden israelilaissiirtokuntalaisten saartaneen hänen seurueensa pakettiauton ja estäneen sen matkan noin 90 minuutiksi miehitetyllä Länsirannalla keskiviikkona. Khannan mukaan siirtokuntalaiset kantoivat yhdysvaltalaisvalmisteisia M4-kiväärejä ja tukkivat seurueen käyttämän tien.

## Seurue vieraili tuhotun kylän raunioilla

Kaliforniaa edustava 49-vuotias Khanna oli alueella tiedonhankintamatkalla, jonka tarkoituksena oli tarkastella Israelin miehityksen vaikutuksia. Seurue vieraili eteläisellä Länsirannalla sijaitsevan Khirbet Zanutan raunioilla. Alueella on lähdeaineiston mukaan tapahtunut toistuvia israelilaissiirtokuntalaisten hyökkäyksiä.

Khanna kertoi Reutersille torstaina, että seurue oli käynyt katsomassa kylää, jonka israelilaissiirtokuntalaiset olivat hänen mukaansa tuhonneet. Hän sanoi myös kylän koulun tuhoutuneen. Vierailun aikana M4-kiväärejä kantaneet siirtokuntalaiset ympäröivät seurueen pakettiauton ja estivät sitä jatkamasta matkaa. Khanna kuvaili kokemusta omakohtaiseksi näkymäksi tilanteisiin, joita miehityksen alaisuudessa elävät palestiinalaiset kohtaavat.

## Tapahtumien kulusta kaksi erilaista kuvausta

Khannan mukaan Israelin asevoimien sotilaat eivät paikalle saavuttuaan puuttuneet tilanteeseen hänen seurueensa hyväksi. Hän kirjoitti viestipalvelu X:ssä sotilaiden asettuneen siirtokuntalaisten puolelle ja jatkaneen seurueen matkan estämistä. Reutersille Khanna sanoi siirtokuntalaisten kutsuneen sotilaat paikalle sen jälkeen, kun tie oli tukittu. Hänen mukaansa asevoimat olivat siirtokuntalaisten eivätkä amerikkalaisten puolella.

Israelin asevoimat esitti tapahtumista toisenlaisen kuvauksen. Sen lausunnon mukaan sotilaat ja poliisit ryhtyivät toimiin saatuaan ilmoituksen, että israelilaiset siviilit olivat tukkineet ajoneuvojen tien alueella. Asevoimien mukaan paikalle saapuneet joukot hajottivat tien tukkineen ryhmän ja antoivat ajoneuvojen jatkaa matkaansa. BBC pyysi Israelin asevoimilta kommenttia Khannan kertomukseen.

Khannan mukaan seurueen matkan estäminen kesti kaikkiaan noin puolitoista tuntia. Lähdeaineistossa ei esitetä riippumatonta vahvistusta koko tapahtumien kululle. Khanna on kahden lapsen isä, ja lähdeaineiston mukaan hän harkitsee ehdokkuutta Yhdysvaltain vuoden 2028 presidentinvaaleissa.

Seurue vieraili Khirbet Zanutan raunioilla selvittämässä Israelin miehityksen vaikutuksia.
Israelin asevoimien mukaan joukot hajottivat tien tukkineet israelilaiset ja päästivät ajoneuvot jatkamaan matkaa.
